done_when: Forge's GitHub reads retry an unreadable or server-error answer a few times with a short pause before giving up, and then say plainly that GitHub didn't answer and to rerun; answers GitHub refuses on purpose (not found, no permission) are not retried; a command test with a faked gh covers one bad answer then a good one (close carries on) and a lasting outage (plain stop)

findings.body: The exhausted-retry message is lost by mandatory reads in `forge merge`. In `src/forge/merge.py:60–69`, a lasting outage during the initial PR lookup turns this failed result into `{}` and tells the user to open or correct the pull request, without mentioning the outage or rerunning. The post-write confirmation at `src/forge/merge.py:94–98` also ignores the read's error and reports that merging is pending. Preserve the plain GitHub-outage refusal in both paths and cover it through the merge command. The supplied close tests pass while these paths remain broken. These required reads are distinct from the optional views whose existing fallbacks the coordinator ruling preserves.
findings.title: Not done: Forge's GitHub reads retry an unreadable or server-error answer a few times with a short pause before giving up, and then say Git

why: One unreadable GitHub answer (an HTML error page: 'invalid character < looking for beginning of value') stops forge close outright outside the checks wait, so a GitHub blip costs a whole rerun (reported by a client session on v1.2.8)
